events.title: August CPI (last major print before FOMC)
events.why_it_matters: The single most important input into the Sept 16 FOMC; consensus near 3.4% y/y headline with oil/war upside risk after a 162k payrolls beat.
events.what_to_watch: Core services and energy passthrough; a hot print hardens the case for the first Fed hike in years.

events.title: FOMC decision, SEP/dot plot, Warsh press conference
events.why_it_matters: Markets price roughly 55-70% odds of a 25bp hike — the first increase in years — after Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole keynote; the dot plot matters more than the decision.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the SEP dots signal one hike or a hiking cycle, and Warsh's reaction function on oil-driven inflation.

events.title: August advance retail sales
events.why_it_matters: July retail sales fell 0.6% m/m, the sharpest drop in over a year; a second weak print would sharpen the stagflation narrative feeding the FOMC.
events.what_to_watch: Control-group sales and whether the consumer is cracking under oil-driven real-income pressure.

events.title: Bank of Japan decision — hike to 1.25% priced
events.why_it_matters: A BOJ hike into a global risk-off, oil-shock backdrop is the classic yen-carry unwind trigger; markets price ~98% odds of a 25bp move to 1.25%.
events.what_to_watch: Ueda's guidance on the pace of further normalization and any JGB yield-control tweaks.

events.title: Bank of England decision — hold at 3.75% expected
events.why_it_matters: BoE is expected to hold at 3.75% after a 6-3 vote in July, but the oil surge has revived hike bets and chief economist Huw Pill has publicly argued for 4%.
events.what_to_watch: The vote split and any hawkish dissent signaling a November hike.

events.title: ECB rate decision — 25bp hike to 2.50% deposit rate delivered
events.why_it_matters: ECB hiked 25bp as expected, citing Middle East conflict inflation pressures; the question now is whether a fourth move is coming.
events.what_to_watch: Lagarde's language on further tightening and the new staff projections path.

events.title: August PPI (pipeline inflation print)
events.why_it_matters: Wholesale prices advanced in line with expectations, keeping the pipeline-inflation narrative intact ahead of CPI.
events.what_to_watch: Whether energy passthrough starts showing in core goods.

events.title: August jobs report — 162k payrolls beat, unemployment 4.1%
events.why_it_matters: A blowout payrolls print removed the labor-market excuse for the Fed to stay on hold, driving hike odds sharply higher.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the resilient labor market keeps the Fed hawkish into year-end.

events.title: Oracle FQ1 2027 earnings — beat, cloud infra +121%
events.why_it_matters: Oracle beat on earnings and revenue with cloud-infrastructure revenue surging 121% and >$30bn in AI contracts, a strong read on AI capex demand.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the AI-infrastructure trade broadens to other cloud and memory names.

events.title: Adobe FQ3 2026 earnings — record Q3, stock slipped
events.why_it_matters: Adobe reported record Q3 results and raised its full-year outlook, but the stock slipped — a bellwether for AI cannibalization of creative-software seats.
events.what_to_watch: Whether AI-native competitors keep pressuring the multiple despite solid fundamentals.

events.title: FedEx FQ1 2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: The best single-company read on global goods demand and parcel pricing, arriving amid tariff-driven trade rerouting and a soft US consumer.
events.what_to_watch: Peak-season guidance and any tariff-related volume commentary.

events.title: Micron FQ4 2026 earnings (AI memory catalyst)
events.why_it_matters: Micron's results are billed as the most important AI-memory catalyst of the year, with HBM pricing and tight supply driving margins.
events.what_to_watch: HBM4 ramp commentary and whether memory pricing strength extends into 2027.

events.title: September quadruple witching / quarterly options expiry
events.why_it_matters: Quarterly expiry of index futures, index options, stock options and single-stock futures lands two days after the FOMC, amplifying volume and pinning risk around a binary macro event.
events.what_to_watch: Dealer gamma positioning and post-FOMC volatility into the close.

events.title: Trump-Xi Washington summit
events.why_it_matters: Xi's state visit to the White House is the highest-stakes trade event of the quarter, covering tariffs, investment, AI, Taiwan and the Iran war — and lands less than six weeks before the US midterms.
events.what_to_watch: Any joint statement on a 'non-sensitive' product list, Taiwan-arms language, or a truce extension.

events.title: US-Iran tanker war; Brent above $108, Hormuz traffic impaired
events.why_it_matters: Iran's largest missile/drone barrage since the April ceasefire, US strikes on Iranian crude carriers, and continued Hormuz disruption have pushed Brent above $108 and diesel to records — a direct stagflationary shock.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Iran's announced 'restricted zone' outside Hormuz materializes and whether US escorts keep oil flowing.

events.title: US-Canada trade war — Section 338 import bans effective Sept 29
events.why_it_matters: Trump's Sept 8 proclamations escalate 50% Section 338 tariffs into outright import bans on Canadian alcohol, dairy and motor vehicles effective Sept 29, with scope changes Sept 15, after Canada's ~$20bn counter-tariffs.
events.what_to_watch: Whether USMCA-exempt supply chains are disrupted and whether Canada retaliates further.

events.title: Canada counter-tariffs on US goods in force
events.why_it_matters: Canada imposed roughly $20bn in retaliatory surtaxes on US goods effective Sept 8, deepening the North American trade rupture.
events.what_to_watch: Which US export sectors absorb the hit and whether talks resume.

events.title: EU moves to curb Chinese chemical/plastics imports
events.why_it_matters: France, Italy and Germany are preparing EU safeguard requests on chemical and plastics imports, and Italy's auto lobby is pushing an 80% tariff above a Chinese-import threshold — a broadening EU-China trade front.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the EU opens formal safeguard investigations in coming weeks.

events.title: Supreme Court IEEPA tariff ruling aftermath — administration rebuilding tariffs
events.why_it_matters: The Supreme Court's February ruling that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs forced the administration to rebuild its tariff program under Section 122/232/338 authorities, creating ongoing legal and refund uncertainty for importers.
events.what_to_watch: CIT appeals and whether new statutory authorities survive legal challenge.

events.title: Section 232 semiconductor tariffs — 25% duties in force
events.why_it_matters: 25% Section 232 duties on semiconductors and derivatives remain in force with a two-phase plan, reshaping chip supply chains and pricing across Asia and US electronics.
events.what_to_watch: Phase-two scope expansion and any Taiwan exemption changes.

events.title: Russia-Ukraine peace talks — Witkoff/Kushner shuttle diplomacy
events.why_it_matters: US envoys met Putin in Moscow and Zelensky in Kyiv, with a temporary halt to long-range strikes — any breakthrough would hit European energy and defense names.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a ceasefire framework emerges and how it interacts with the Iran oil shock.

events.title: UN General Assembly high-level week / General Debate
events.why_it_matters: UNGA 81 General Debate from Sept 22 will be dominated by Iran, Ukraine, climate finance and trade, with side-deal and headline risk.
events.what_to_watch: Any Iran or Ukraine diplomatic breakthrough announced on the margins.

events.title: US midterm elections — policy stakes building
events.why_it_matters: The Nov 3 midterms will determine how much economic policy can change over the next two years; positioning and policy-uncertainty premium build through the fall.
events.what_to_watch: Polling shifts on House/Senate control and their read-through to tax, tariff and healthcare policy.

events.title: Government funding — CR through Dec 11 averts Oct 1 shutdown
events.why_it_matters: Trump signed a stopgap continuing resolution funding the government at current levels through Dec 11, removing near-term shutdown risk but setting up a December fight.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the December 11 deadline becomes a midterm-season brinkmanship event.

events.title: Northern Europe port strikes — Rotterdam/Germany disruption
events.why_it_matters: Rotterdam and German dockworker walkouts disrupted container and vessel handling across Northern Europe, adding to global freight friction.
events.what_to_watch: Whether labor actions spread or a wage deal restores throughput.

events.title: South Korea/Japan semiconductor investment wave — Samsung Yokohama hub, SK Hynix Japan plant
events.why_it_matters: Samsung opened a Yokohama chip R&D hub and SK Hynix is weighing a Miyagi memory plant, deepening Korea-Japan semiconductor integration amid record Korean chip exports.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the AI-memory boom keeps KOSPI/Nikkei chip names leading global equities.

events.title: Gold safe-haven bid toward record highs
events.why_it_matters: Gold is surging toward $4,500 as investors seek safe havens from war, inflation and Fed-hike risk — a barometer of macro stress.
events.what_to_watch: Whether a hawkish FOMC triggers a sharp gold correction or accelerates the bid.

events.title: AI Infra Summit / semiconductor conference season
events.why_it_matters: The AI Infra Summit in Santa Clara (Sept 15-17) and adjacent EDA/cloud events concentrate AI-datacenter demand signals for chip and infrastructure names.
events.what_to_watch: Any new accelerator, HBM or networking announcements that move semis.

events.title: September PDUFA cluster — 11 FDA decisions
events.why_it_matters: September is the busiest PDUFA month of H2 with 11 FDA target action dates across rare disease, oncology, neurology and hematology — binary catalysts for small- and mid-cap biotech.
events.what_to_watch: Approvals or CRLs in rare-disease programs (Sanfilippo, Alexander disease, A-T, MCT8).

events.title: Atlantic hurricane season — below-normal but mid-month Southeast risk
events.why_it_matters: Forecasters call for a well-below-normal season under El Niño, but AccuWeather flags a risk of tropical development near the Southeast coast around mid-month.
events.what_to_watch: Any named storm tracking toward Gulf energy infrastructure or the US East Coast.

events.title: Anthropic IPO preparation — Morgan Stanley/Goldman lead roles
events.why_it_matters: Anthropic is preparing to name Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs to lead its IPO, a potential mega-listing that would test AI-valuation appetite.
events.what_to_watch: Filing timing and any valuation range that resets AI private-market marks.

events.title: US housing/mortgage data — rates near cycle highs
events.why_it_matters: Housing starts, building permits and existing-home sales land around the FOMC; a hike would push mortgage rates higher into an already-fragile housing market.
events.what_to_watch: Whether higher rates freeze transaction volumes further.

top_risks: Sept 16 FOMC delivers a hawkish hike with dots signaling more, triggering a broad risk-off repricing across equities, credit and real estate.
Oil shock escalation: Iran's 'restricted zone' outside Hormuz or a wider US-Iran exchange pushes Brent well above $110, deepening stagflation.
BOJ hike (Sept 16-17) into a risk-off backdrop sparks a yen-carry unwind and global deleveraging.
US-Canada Section 338 import bans (Sept 29) and EU-China chemical safeguards broaden the trade war and hit industrials/materials.
Trump-Xi summit (Sept 24) fails or produces Taiwan-arms friction, reigniting tariff escalation into the midterms.
top_opportunities: AI-infrastructure and memory names (Oracle beat, Micron Sept 30, Samsung/SK Hynix capex) if the AI capex cycle keeps beating.
Gold and defensive/energy longs as a hedge against war-driven inflation and Fed-hike risk.
A soft CPI today could cap hike odds and spark a relief rally in rate-sensitive cyclicals and small caps.
Russia-Ukraine ceasefire progress would lift European equities and compress energy risk premia.
Biotech binary catalysts from the September PDUFA cluster for event-driven traders.
summary: The scan is dominated by a live September FOMC (Sept 16) with hike odds near 55-70% after a blowout August payrolls print, a hot PPI and today's CPI, and an oil shock from the US-Iran tanker war keeping Brent above $108. Central bank decisions from the BOJ (Sept 16-17) and BoE (Sept 17) cluster around the Fed after the ECB hiked 25bp on Sept 10, while a heavy earnings slate (Oracle beat, Adobe, FedEx, Micron) and the Sept 24 Trump-Xi summit add idiosyncratic and geopolitical risk. North American trade tensions escalated with Canada's counter-tariffs in force and US Section 338 import bans due Sept 29, and Sept 18 quadruple witching amplifies positioning risk around the FOMC.
